summary: A 1929 Aermotor MC-24 lookout on Rose Peak in Arizona's Apache-Sitgreaves forest, with its cab replaced in 1981; sources disagree on its height and build year.

facts.design: Aermotor MC-24 cab on a steel tower; cab replaced in 1981 with a 14x14 ft R-6 wood flat-top live-in cab with catwalk

access.note: The register lists an active Forest Service station. Whether visitors may enter the cab is not confirmed.

visit.trail_note: A closed dirt road leads to the top, per an undated trip report

events.note: Aermotor MC-24 lookout built to replace several earlier wood platform towers; a 1929 USFS photo shows it under construction. A 1928 newspaper item already calls the steel tower recently completed.
Original 12x12 ft cab replaced with a 14x14 ft R-6 wood flat-top live-in cab with catwalk
Registered March 4, 2002 as US 423, AZ 30; nominated by Dave Lorenz

corrections.why: No source gives 91.4 m for the tower. 91.4 m is 300 ft, and the only 300-foot figure in the sources is a slope in a 1928 newspaper account. The register gives a 30 ft tower (9.1 m). Forest Lookouts gives 20 ft, and the NGS station description it quotes gives about 50 ft overall, so the human editor should check which figure to keep.

notes_for_editor: Record height 91.4 m (300 ft) matches no source; see corrections. Build year: the register and a 1929 USFS photo say 1929, but a 1928 newspaper item quoted by Forest Lookouts calls the steel tower recently completed. Left at 1929, unresolved. Staffing and cab access are unconfirmed: the register's active-service line is undated, and the rangeoflight.net trip note is undated. The photo url is the Flickr page, not the direct image file, which I did not extract. Forest Service picnic-site page read: no lookout content. HikeArizona returned 403, so the trail distance is unverified and not used. Access level set to unknown: no source gives a restriction, so the earlier restricted value was unsupported.
